# Verification and dependencies

## Reproduce the checks

After obtaining the dependency cache as described in
[Using the library](Using-the-library), run:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'
python3 tools/project_sources.py
python3 tools/wiki_docs.py check
python3 tools/five_constrained/generate_catalogue.py --check
python3 tools/five_constrained/generate_certificates.py --check
lake --rehash build
lake env lean docs/Examples.lean
lake env lean docs/CheckTheoremMap.lean
lake env lean Hypertournaments/AxiomAudit.lean
```

The source checker verifies facade coverage, specific imports and the pinned
vendored source closure. The documentation checker resolves the registered
declarations to their defining files, checks page links and detects stale
generated pages. `docs/CheckTheoremMap.lean` checks that the fully qualified
names in the correspondence remain available through the library import.

The finite catalogue and certificate checks reproduce the retained data.
The Lean build checks the resulting mathematical proofs in the kernel.

## Axiom boundary

CI also runs the pinned complete defining-module axiom audit over every
project and vendored declaration reachable through the library. Its
allowlist is Lean's standard `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
Source checks reject proof placeholders and custom axioms. The readable
[`Hypertournaments/AxiomAudit.lean`](https://github.com/shulda/hypertournaments/blob/97ece7669d91ffeff83227cc2d2b8cd64f141bfd/Hypertournaments/AxiomAudit.lean) supplies selected endpoint prints
in addition to the complete audit.

When citing a result, retain a checked release tag or commit together with
the declaration name. Source-file links and the paper-label correspondence
make the exact assumptions available for inspection. The
[publishing guide](Publishing) explains how to generate links for a fixed
revision.

## Dependencies and attribution

The Lean and Mathlib versions are fixed by [`lean-toolchain`](https://github.com/shulda/hypertournaments/blob/97ece7669d91ffeff83227cc2d2b8cd64f141bfd/lean-toolchain),
[`lakefile.toml`](https://github.com/shulda/hypertournaments/blob/97ece7669d91ffeff83227cc2d2b8cd64f141bfd/lakefile.toml) and [`lake-manifest.json`](https://github.com/shulda/hypertournaments/blob/97ece7669d91ffeff83227cc2d2b8cd64f141bfd/lake-manifest.json). The project also
retains the required partite/Ramsey proof sources, including Jan Hubička's
[PartiteConstruction](https://github.com/janhubicka/partite-construction)
and [SuccessorTree](https://github.com/janhubicka/lean-successors) libraries.
Their retained source notices, provenance and supplied license text accompany
the vendored files. The source-integrity check validates that snapshot.

The formalization was developed with extensive AI assistance. The trusted
mathematical boundary is the recorded Lean statements and their kernel-checked
proofs; the three reference chapters explain their correspondence with the
human expositions.
